$comment: Bead's interop service: the procedures every implementation's interop server offers alike, so a client of one calls a server of another, and the conversations of conversations.json play against any of them.
Payloads are JSON, in UTF-8, written without a space. A payload that is not JSON is answered with PAYLOAD_UNDECODABLE.
answers says what a procedure answers; admits, what its admission lets through, when it has one.
offeredBy client: a command, which a client offers and its server calls; any other procedure, the server offers.
notifies: what a notification procedure notifies its subscribers.
relay: what the interop server's relay admits. Its destinations are its clients' connections, each registered by register and taken out by unregister.

relay.admits: a connection with a session, as section 14.3 has a server's relay ask by default; any other is refused with SESSION_REQUIRED

procedures.answers: its request's payload, the same value
an application failure: code 7, detail "this procedure fails, on purpose"
n, once n milliseconds passed; cancelled first, it counts one cancellation for its connection, then answers n all the same, an answer that must not go out
how many calls to slow its connection cancelled so far, a number

procedures.admits: nobody: every request is refused with ACCESS_DENIED, detail "this procedure admits nobody"

procedures.answers: nothing: it throws "this procedure breaks, on purpose" before it answers, which its server answers with PROCEDURE_FAILED and reports
a string of n letters x
what its client's clock answers, asked "What time is it where you are?" within 10 s; a clock that fails fails it, answered with PROCEDURE_FAILED

procedures.notifies: each value tick notifies, as a JSON number, on its connection
procedures.answers: null: at once; or, held, once n ticks of its connection notified, having subscribed its requester before it waits; held and failing, an application failure there instead: code 7, detail "this procedure fails, on purpose"
null, once it notified v to its connection's subscription to ticks — keyed by k when given — and the ticks it held have answered

s, once it opened a new session for its connection, s its data, its session timeout t and its connection timeout c, each held as section 1.4 holds a duration and without end when not given (section 13.7); a t or c under a millisecond or past 2³¹ − 1, as given, opens no session and fails it, which its server answers with PROCEDURE_FAILED and reports

procedures.admits: a connection with a session; any other is refused with SESSION_REQUIRED
procedures.answers: null, once it ended its connection's session

procedures.admits: a connection with a session; any other is refused with SESSION_REQUIRED
procedures.answers: the name its connection's session holds

n, once it registered its caller's connection as the destination n, leg B waiting t milliseconds at most for its answer when given, t held as section 1.4 holds a duration; a t under a millisecond or past 2³¹ − 1, as given, registers nothing and fails it, which its server answers with PROCEDURE_FAILED and reports; a destination registered already fails it, an application failure: code 8, detail "that destination is registered already"
true, once it took out the destination its caller's connection registered last; false when there is none, or another took its id since
